newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian All Ordinaries still suspect.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian All Ordinaries still suspect.

text.p: The Australian All Ordinaries bounces from 2,600 and possibly will move higher.

Short and longer term leading indicators are in conflict, so traders will be cautious and tentative while between 2,600 and 2,700. Fibonacci retracements can take the index to 2700, but seasoned traders are likely to wait to see if there is enough to push it higher.
Short-term technicals are mixed. Averages are bearish. Ten-day has moved lower through 20-day, and price is below all three. Leading indicators and Bollinger bands are oversold.
Leading indicators have turned up from being oversold, and are moving higher.
Fibonacci retracements are, 2,658 (reached), 2,675 and 2,692.
Medium term the index displayed a dramatic one week fall, but finished with a strong recovery.
While above 2,650, traders are likely to be focusing on higher levels, but wary of resistance at 2,700.
Medium-term technicals are mixed, but reverse of the short term.
Averages are moving higher. Price has fallen through 10 week, so traders are likely to be circumspect, as this average could turn lower.
Bollinger Bands show the index is still overbought.
Leading indicators remain overbought and moving lower.
ROC decline is strongest decline, with the RSI and Stochastics beginning to turn. Stochastics have crossed lower.
Lower Fibonacci retracements lower are 2,598 (reached 2,604), 2,549 and 2,500.
Longer term, the index is below July's high and resistance at 2,700 and 2,740. There is a potential bearish pivot point reversal.
If the index can not regain 2,740, traders are likely to be considering liquidating long positions.
Longer term support is some way off at 2,350, so traders are likely to be using shorter term levels.
Longer term technicals are mixed and overbought. Averages remain bullish.
All leading indicators are overbought and moving lower. Stochastics still very overbought and lower again at 91/93.
Seasoned traders will not be blinded by the aggressive buying last Friday.
The index is lower, indicators are overbought in the medium and longer terms. There is resistance at 2,700 and 2,740/60. While below these level the index is technically bearish.
Elliot Wavers see the rally to 2,757 as a fifth wave - if not it is still an overbought extension of the rally.
The last six weeks is the a-b-c correction, which is a pre-cursor to a further fall. Remain cautious while below 2,700.

The index has bounced from 2,600 (m/t Fibonacci level). Short term indicators are favouring a further rally, especially with the index finishing strongly. This bear market rally can easily move to 2,700.
Until it breaks it is still a bear market rally, and should be treated with caution.
(Daniel Fock is a member of the Australian Technical Analysts Association. Views are his own.)
